newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk says union agrees to drop strike plans.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk says union agrees to drop strike plans.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group said on Tuesday in a news release that the trade union strike committee at the company's flagship plant had agreed not to disrupt production or loading of metals through June 30.

Plans by workers at the flagship plant to disrupt output on March 27 -- a day of nationwide protests -- and April 2 had been dropped, it said, adding that workers would still protest on March 27 but would do so vocally and not disrupt output.
It said workers had decided to show solidarity with other industry workers on March 27 in a bid to draw the government's attention to social problems in the Arctic North.

Moscow union leaders say more than 20 million protesters, backed by Russia's communist opposition, are expected to join a nationwide protest on Thursday to complain about massive backlogs in wage and pension payments.

"The strike coordinating committee of the Norilsk mining and metallurgical combine has obliged itself in the period before July 1 not to conduct any strikes or similar actions related to halting output or stopping the unloading of metals (for export)," the release said.

"Thus the strike called for April 2 will not take place. Both sides (management and labour) have agreed that the action planned by the strike committee for March 27 will be directed towards attracting the attention of the President, the government and other federal organs to the social problems of inhabitants of the Norilsk industrial region."
